description: Backend for FR-20: persist which tutorials each account has seen and expose an idempotent endpoint to mark them. Independent of the frontend features; it only adds a field, a migration, a serializer, a view, a URL, an admin fieldset, and tests. Per doc section 3 and the doc 2.5 default (migration marks only 'cliente' seen for users with last_login; no admin.* keys).
steps: In backend/apps/accounts/models.py, add module-level TUTORIALES tuple with exactly these keys in order: 'cliente','admin.bienvenida','admin.panel','admin.productos','admin.producto-formulario','admin.promociones','admin.pedidos','admin.pedido-detalle','admin.usuarios','admin.estadisticas'; add TUTORIALES_ADMIN = tuple(c for c in TUTORIALES if c.startswith('admin.')). Add field to Usuario: tutoriales_vistos = models.JSONField('tutoriales vistos', default=list, blank=True).

Create backend/apps/accounts/migrations/0002_usuario_tutoriales_vistos.py by hand: dependencies=[('accounts','0001_initial')]; operations = AddField(model_name='usuario', name='tutoriales_vistos', field=models.JSONField(default=list, blank=True, verbose_name='tutoriales vistos')) then migrations.RunPython(forward, migrations.RunPython.noop). forward(apps, schema_editor): Usuario = apps.get_model('accounts','Usuario'); for each user with last_login not null, set tutoriales_vistos=['cliente'] and save(update_fields=['tutoriales_vistos']).
In backend/apps/accounts/admin.py, add a fieldset ('Tutoriales', {'fields': ('tutoriales_vistos',)}) to UsuarioAdmin.fieldsets (e.g. after 'Fechas') so staff can reset it when testing.

In backend/apps/accounts/serializers.py, append 'tutoriales_vistos' to UsuarioSerializer.Meta.fields (read_only_fields = fields, so it stays read-only). Add TutorialVistoSerializer(serializers.Serializer) with claves = serializers.ListField(child=serializers.ChoiceField(choices=TUTORIALES), allow_empty=False); import TUTORIALES from .models.

In backend/apps/accounts/views.py, add TutorialVistoView(APIView) exactly per doc 3.4: default IsAuthenticated; post() validates TutorialVistoSerializer, merges claves into set(usuario.tutoriales_vistos), stores sorted(...), save(update_fields=['tutoriales_vistos']), returns UsuarioSerializer(usuario).data. Import TutorialVistoSerializer.
In backend/apps/accounts/urls.py, import TutorialVistoView and add path('tutoriales/vistos/', TutorialVistoView.as_view(), name='tutoriales-vistos'). The app is mounted under /api/auth/.

Create backend/tests/test_tutoriales.py covering doc 3.5, following tests/test_accounts.py style and the api fixture in tests/conftest.py: quien-soy/ and login/ include tutoriales_vistos (empty for a new account); POST one valid key adds it (200); repeated POST does not duplicate; POST several keys adds all; POST an invalid key returns 400 and stores nothing; POST without session returns 403; endpoint only touches request.user; data-migration behavior: user with last_login gets ['cliente'], user without stays empty (test the migration forward function by importing it, or via django_test_migrations only if already installed).
acceptance_criteria: `pytest tests/test_tutoriales.py` from backend/ passes all new tests
`pytest` full suite from backend/ stays green
`python manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run` reports no pending changes after 0002 is written
POST /api/auth/tutoriales/vistos/ with {"claves":["admin.productos"]} returns 200 with the updated user; an unknown key returns 400; no session returns 403
findings:
Backend done. Contract for the frontend:
- Field apps.accounts.models.Usuario.tutoriales_vistos (JSONField, default=list). Values are stored sorted() and deduplicated.
- apps.accounts.models.TUTORIALES (10 keys, doc order) and TUTORIALES_ADMIN (the 9 'admin.*' keys) are the canonical key lists; the frontend ClaveTutorial union must match TUTORIALES exactly.
- UsuarioSerializer now returns tutoriales_vistos (read-only), so login/ and quien-soy/ already include it. Frontend core/models/usuario.ts needs tutoriales_vistos: string[].
- Endpoint: POST /api/auth/tutoriales/vistos/ body {"claves": ["admin.productos", ...]}. IsAuthenticated. Returns 200 with the full updated UsuarioSerializer payload; 400 if any key is not in TUTORIALES (nothing stored); 403 without session. Idempotent (merges into a set). allow_empty=False, so an empty claves list is a 400.
- Migration 0002_usuario_tutoriales_vistos.py (hand-written) adds the field and has a RunPython forward that sets ['cliente'] for users with last_login not null (reverse=noop). Its forward() is importable for tests via importlib (module name starts with a digit).
- Admin: UsuarioAdmin has a 'Tutoriales' fieldset so staff can reset tutoriales_vistos when testing.
- Verified on this commit: pytest tests/test_tutoriales.py (9 passed), full pytest (247 passed), makemigrations --check --dry-run (no changes), ruff check apps/accounts (clean).
